title: modernize-commit-coordinator-and-kv-prefetch-strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Legacy commit coordinator creates a global contention point during high-concurrency continuous batching workloads and holds epoch-level locks while the KV prefetch path performs synchronous disk-backed refills. This ticket rewrites the commit/lease machinery to remove global locking, introduce fine-grained per-shard fencing tokens, and replace the synchronous prefetch heuristic with an adaptive, decay-based predictor. Goals: reduce tail latency under bursty traffic by 20% p95, cut GC/heap pressure caused by simultaneous refills, and eliminate jitter caused by coordinator backoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Commit coordinator rewritten to use per-shard token fencing (no global mutex) and can be exercised under load with no correctness regressions
KV prefetch path uses decay-based LRU predictor with configurable thresholds and avoids synchronous disk reads on the hot path
End-to-end latency: p95 improvement >= 15% and p99 improvement >= 10% in the benchmark harness for mixed short/long sequences
Regression tests and integration tests added; CI coverage for lease handoff, prefetch races, and slot preemption
Deployment can be rolled out incrementally via canary flag and has automatic fallback to previous coordinator on error
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed comparing global lock vs token fencing designs; microbenchmarks show token fencing reduces lock contention by ~40%.
2026-02-18: Prototype committed for per-shard token allocator; initial race discovered when a prefetch completes after lease expiry — added a validation step to drop stale tokens.
2026-02-24: New decay-based prefetch predictor implemented; tunable 'decay_window_ms' exposed in runtime config. Early staging runs show 12% p95 reduction on short-sequence workload.
2026-02-28: Integration tests for lease handoff and slot preemption added; discovered a memory leak in the token map during extreme churn — fixed via weak refs and explicit reclamation.
2026-03-01: Internal load test (1k qps) shows reduced p99 jitter but a regression in throughput for very long-sequence streams; investigating backpressure interaction with the prefetch limiter.
risks: Prefetch heuristic may under-admit cold keys leading to increased tail disk IO for low-reuse workloads
Token fencing introduces more metadata and may increase heap usage if reclamation paths have gaps
Behavioral differences under dedicated vs hosted deployments (differences in disk latency) could surface only in customer environments
Rollback complexity: partial rollout where some pods run new coordinator and others old could expose version skew bugs
testing_plan: Unit tests for token lifecycle, fence validation, and stale-token drop paths
Integration scenarios: lease handoff during prefetch completion, slot preemption with in-flight KV reads
Deterministic replay harness with recorded traffic from three customers to validate no correctness regressions
Performance suite: short-seq heavy concurrency, mixed seq length, and long-seq dominance runs with detailed telemetry
Chaos tests: kill coordinator pod mid-prefetch, network partition between shard owners, and simulated disk latency spikes
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated deploy to canary pool (5% traffic) for 48h with p95/p99 monitors
If stable, expand to 30% and run 72h soak with SLA checks and heap/GC dashboards
30-minute rollback policy on elevated error rates or >10% latency regression vs baseline
Final cutover scheduled during low-traffic window with runbook for manual migration of lease metadata if automatic handoff fails
notes: Decision: prefer token fencing over epoch bumping to reduce coordination churn (recorded 2026-02-12)
Follow-up: evaluate persistent token cache for extremely bursty workloads (post-launch)
Related: coordinate with infra team to add a small histogram for token creation rate to console dashboards
